title: One output, one sub-problem
idea: MEET: the simplest split starts from the outputs — each thing the problem asks for usually becomes its own sub-problem.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: 'Show the total and the average of the scores.' Starting from outputs, how many sub-problems?
options: Two — one for the total, one for the average
exercises.explanation: Two outputs (total, average) suggest two sub-problems to start. Each output earns its own piece.

exercises.prompt: A good first split is 'one sub-problem per output the problem asks for'.
exercises.explanation: Yes — listing outputs from Unit 85 gives you a starter list of sub-problems for free.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: 'Count the passes and count the fails.' The two sub-problems are...
options: count the passes; count the fails
exercises.explanation: Two outputs, two sub-problems: one count for passes, one for fails. Each output maps to a job.

exercises.prompt: Select the sub-problems for 'show the biggest price and the smallest price'.
exercises.explanation: Two outputs become two tracking sub-problems: biggest and smallest. The others aren't jobs the problem needs.

exercises.prompt: Why start the split from the OUTPUTS?
options: Each thing you must produce is naturally its own piece of work
exercises.explanation: Every output is something you must build, so each is a ready-made sub-problem. It's the easiest place to start.

exercises.prompt: Two outputs always collapse into a single sub-problem.
exercises.explanation: No — usually each output is its own job. Sometimes they share a step, but start by giving each its own piece.

exercises.prompt: Match each output to its sub-problem job.

pairs.right: count items that pass the rule

exercises.explanation: Each output names a familiar job. The output IS the hint for which pattern the sub-problem needs.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: 'Report the average and whether it passed (>=60).' The two sub-problems are...
options: compute the average; decide pass/fail from the average
exercises.explanation: Average is one job; deciding pass/fail (average >= 60) is a second job that uses the first's result.

blocks: List every output the problem asks for
Give each output its own sub-problem
Note if any sub-problem needs another's result
exercises.explanation: List outputs, make each a sub-problem, then spot dependencies. A clean starter decomposition.

options: Start the split from the outputs — one sub-problem per thing you must produce
exercises.explanation: Outputs first. Each thing the problem asks for is a natural sub-problem — the easiest way to begin splitting.
